about: Capture-time provenance for docs/screens/*.png (#335). One row per shot, written by the session that took the pixels: sha256/canvas are properties of the bytes, origin/install/url/seed/level/layout/sampleRate/build are properties of the instrument and cannot be recovered from the PNG afterwards. `node tools/recap.js check` verifies each row against the file it addresses and against every other row of the same (seed, level, sampleRate); the vocabulary, the route verdicts and the audio-draw rule live in tools/recap.js, not here.
plan: Shared by all six shots and recorded in README.md's capture block: window 1440x763 on the deployed build at ?dev=1&seed=60, DEV.boot(); DEV.freeze(true); DEV.tick(30), then DEV.cam(...) and one DEV.tick(1) per shot, vitals pinned at 100, the level's own hostiles cleared (never DEV.clear()), level banner taken down with banner('', 0). A frozen clock does not stop S.t, so these frames are reproducible by statistics and never by md5. **One term this plan did not record: the audio device.** A live boot advances the seeded stream through SND.init's noise buffer before the generator runs, so one seed deals one level per sample rate (#404, and the rule the tool prints as HW_WHY). These six captures read no SND.ac.sampleRate, so every row carries `sampleRate: null`, `check` prints each one as a device-scoped deal, and the binding below is per-machine: it says this frame is what ?dev=1&seed=60 dealt on the capture's audio device, not that every machine deals it. `STRICT=1 node tools/recap.js check` gates the missing term. A capture that reads the rate turns its own row into a cross-machine binding with no change to the tool.

shots.note: Deal transcribed from README.md's capture block, which names all six shots as one route: the deployed page opened at ?dev=1&seed=60, build proved by eval-visible code markers, every deployed js blob md5-identical to the tree at ce9d39d. layout is that block's DEV.layoutSig() for the deal. Pose: one posed grunt 6 m out on the camera's own band (a posed body added with DEV.spawn, never DEV.clear, which would leave 0 LEFT on the HUD).

The reference shot for the block: the route and every deal field in these six rows are transcribed from README.md's capture block (deployed build, ?dev=1&seed=60, DEV.layoutSig 735688443, js blobs md5-identical to ce9d39d) rather than re-measured here. #335 measured this route: reloading the same URL read DEV.seed 60 and layout 735688443 on both loads, which is what makes origin+install=url-open a binding route.

Re-taken at fc7a555 (#388, fifth frame for this seat) because #19's footprint blend landed on main while this row was in review. This PR changes no js/, so the renderer the merge ships is main's, and a caption cannot name one the merged tree does not have. The deployed page already serves that renderer: index.html 44b7f0ca and all eleven js/ blobs read over the wire at this head are md5-identical to this merged tree - js/40_render.js 60af7c97, js/90_dev.js 7c2373a3 (it adds DEV's gndfade switch), js/20_level.js 5792aeb3, js/13_mesh.js c2f9a53 - so route, served page and tree name one build, which is the claim this row exists to make. Route is unchanged and is the URL itself: headless Chromium opened this row's url at a 1440x763 device-metrics override at scale 1 and, once the page reported ready, ran DEV.boot(); startLevel(3, true); banner('', 0); DEV.freeze(true); DEV.tick(30); P.hp = 100; DEV.cam(1.5, 2.5, floorAt(1.5, 2.5), 0.60, 0); DEV.tick(1), leaving the level's own 4 hostiles standing. S.mode read 'play' at all four probes in both runs. The blur rule the previous row recorded still holds - a page that never acquires a pointer lock pauses on the first blur and the overlay dims everything under it, so the route ends with the game's own resume() plus one DEV.tick(1) and re-reads S.mode immediately before the shutter, which is also why the route runs after ready rather than from a document-time script. Two runs of that route at this head BOTH read DEV.layoutSig() 2733654509, the value this row has always carried, so this frame's deal is reproducible at this build; the same route at the PREVIOUS deployed build read 3233039185 twice and, issued several seconds after ready, 1900969947, and startLevel(3, true) called twice inside one already-open page read 1730990788 then 1523817166. startLevel generates from wherever the seeded stream has reached and generation advances it, so the deal a run lands on is a property of the run and of the build that ran it, not of the url - pinning the stream before startLevel (#420) is still the only way to make a stored frame re-takeable and a deal number re-readable. DEV.state().gnd now reads fade 1 beside jit 1, light 1, ax 1, filt 1, ramp 1, far 1, jitMinPx 48, axMin 1.5, mipax 1, mipar 4; DECOR reads 14 and FIX_DEP {DOOR 0.12, PIPE 0.10, STRIPE 0.03, VENT 0.08} as before, so #400's stood-off fixture is still a term of these pixels. props 9, lights 7, sr 44100, buf 678x359 upscaled to a 1440x763 canvas. Against the bytes this row replaces (94022ea3, drawn at 8eade8f): mean 50.54 -> 50.50, thirds 41.85 / 58.94 / 50.87 -> 41.82 / 58.88 / 50.83, channels 49.6 / 51.1 / 47.7 unchanged, 0 rows below luma 24 in both. 78,954 of 1,098,720 px move by more than 2 luma (4,793 / 45,098 / 29,063 by thirds), worst 23.6, mean |delta| 0.57, sitting in rows 400-600 - the lit floor in front of the TECH wall and the wall's lower face - while rows 300-330 read 38.2 in both, rows 140-180 44.7 in both, the x 660-1295 x y 340-422 band 83.2 in both, and every row-mean third delta rounds to 0.00-0.05. The term was measured in the live page rather than argued: the same route at the same build with DEV.set('gndfade', 0) applied before the shutter comes back to 6,474 px over 2 luma, worst 11.0, mean |delta| 0.16 and 0.00 in every row-mean third - against 6,048 px worst 5.9 for two runs of the route with the shipped switch. So #19's blend is the whole move and what is left is the route's own noise floor; the deal did not move (layout 2733654509 both sides), which is what a renderer term looks like in a caption that has been reading deal moves. Two runs at one build are not byte-identical even so - they differ in 157,631 px by up to 6 in one channel - so this sha256 names THIS capture, not every run of the route. SND.ac.sampleRate read 44100, so this row is a cross-machine binding where the other five are device-scoped.
